decided.rationale: Branch protection is a configuration of the repository itself that guards branch history against direct or forced changes, so it follows the repository and not any deployment fact. None of production, internet_exposed, contains_customer_data or ai_enabled says whether a repository has branch history worth protecting, so none of them gives a sound exemption. Proposing no rule claims that branch protection applies to every archived repository snapshot, and the frozen nature of a snapshot cannot be expressed with the four usable fields.

decided.rationale: Pull request review is a practice about how changes are accepted into a repository, and the evidence for it lives in the merge history that a snapshot still carries. Whether the target is production, internet exposed, holds customer data or is AI enabled does not change whether its changes should have been reviewed, so none of the four fields gives a sound exemption. Proposing no rule therefore claims that pull request review applies to every archived repository snapshot.

decided.rationale: Protected release tags keep the mapping between a version label and a commit from being altered, which is an integrity property of the repository history and not of a deployment. decided.rationale: Disaster recovery testing exercises the recovery of a running service, and the approved definition of production states that recovery controls are in play when the target is used as, or supports, a production system. When production is KNOWN_FALSE the target neither is nor supports a production system, so there is no production recovery to test and the control does not apply. A snapshot that serves as a recovery source for a production system would be production KNOWN_TRUE and the control would then resolve as applicable, and an UNKNOWN value leaves applicability unresolved.
